dimensions.note: No credentials: all three endpoints are public. The ntfy topic lives in the user's vault and is consumed by @mgreten/ntfy-notify, not this extension.
Info on entry (providers read) and completion (open/new/resolved counts), warning per unreachable provider, structured placeholders throughout.

Per-provider failures (HTTP status, timeout, unparseable body) are recorded on that provider rather than thrown, by design: one slow page must not hide the other two. The method throws before any write when every provider fails. HTTP errors record the status, not the body.

21 tests against real responses saved 2026-10-28: parsing, UTF-16 decoding, region filter, new/resolved detection, single and consecutive provider outages, the method with stubbed fetch (success, one 503, garbled body, all unreachable with no writes), and the report's success, failed-run and missing-summary paths.

Read-only. New-incident state carries across unreachable checks (a bug where two consecutive failures re-alerted on recovery was found in this review and fixed, with a regression test). Removing a provider or region from config makes its incidents read as resolved, and re-adding makes them new again; that is intended.

Statuspage summary.json is documented; the AWS currentevents feed is public but undocumented, so its shape is validated (must be an array) and a format change reads as unreachable rather than all clear. Bodies are read whole; the largest (Cloudflare) is about 230 KB. No pagination or rate limits apply to one GET per check.
Non-OK response bodies are cancelled; every fetch has a timeout combined with the run's abort signal. Nothing is created outside swamp data.
Fixtures are trimmed public status responses with no private identifiers; README uses public endpoints and a vault reference for the ntfy topic. No IP literals.
Plain z.object schemas, no passthrough; every field the workflow reads by CEL (newIncidentCount, alertTitle, alertMessage, alertPriority, checkedAt) is declared.
provider: 30d, 50 versions. summary: infinite, 50 versions, since it carries the seen-incident state the next check compares against.
Read-only status reader; it manages no resource.
provider-github, provider-cloudflare, provider-aws and summary; unique across specs.
